single_key_example.description: Example of a simple test case checking a single key/property
single_key_example.natural_language: Verify the build task has status 'Succeeded'.
single_key_example.rego_code:
deny contains result if {
    some attestation in input.attestations
    some task in attestation.statement.predicate.buildConfig.tasks
    task.name == "build"
    task.status != "Succeeded"
    result := sprintf("Build task status is %s, expected Succeeded", [task.status])
}
single_key_example.notes: This is a simple test case that checks a single property (task.status) after filtering by task name. Note: Always starts with 'some attestation in input.attestations'.

compound_example.description: Example of a compound test case checking multiple keys across all tasks
compound_example.natural_language: Verify all tasks in the PipelineRun attestation have a bundle reference with a digest (contains @sha256:).
compound_example.rego_code:
deny contains result if {
    some attestation in input.attestations
    some task in attestation.statement.predicate.buildConfig.tasks
    bundle := task.ref.bundle
    bundle
    not contains(bundle, "@sha256:")
    result := sprintf("Task %s uses bundle without digest: %s", [task.name, bundle])
}
compound_example.notes: This is a compound test case that loops over ALL tasks (not filtering by name) and checks multiple properties (bundle existence and digest presence) for each task. Note: Always starts with 'some attestation in input.attestations'.

compound_with_parameters_example.description: Example of compound test case checking parameters across all tasks
compound_with_parameters_example.natural_language: Verify all tasks that have a 'mode' parameter do not have it set to 'permissive'.
compound_with_parameters_example.notes: This compound test case loops over all tasks and checks if any task has a specific parameter value, without filtering by task name first. Note: Always starts with 'some attestation in input.attestations'.

variable_naming_example.description: Example showing correct variable naming to avoid reuse
variable_naming_example.natural_language: Verify that the build task has a result named 'IMAGE_URL' with a non-empty value.
variable_naming_example.rego_code_correct:
deny contains result if {
    some attestation in input.attestations
    some task in attestation.statement.predicate.buildConfig.tasks
    task.name == "build"
    some task_result in task.results
    task_result.name == "IMAGE_URL"
    task_result.value == ""
    result := "Build task IMAGE_URL result is empty"
}
variable_naming_example.rego_code_incorrect:
deny contains result if {
    some attestation in input.attestations
    some task in attestation.statement.predicate.buildConfig.tasks
    task.name == "build"
    some result in task.results
    result.name == "IMAGE_URL"
    result := "Build task IMAGE_URL result is empty"
}
variable_naming_example.explanation: The incorrect version reuses 'result' - first as loop variable, then as output. The correct version uses 'task_result' for the loop variable and 'result' only for the output.
variable_naming_rules: Output variable: Always use 'result' for the deny output
Any intermediate variable: Use descriptive names like 'bundle', 'timestamp', 'value' (NOT 'result')

summary.required_pattern: ALL rules must start with: some attestation in input.attestations
summary.variable_naming_rule: NEVER reuse 'result' - it's reserved for the deny output. Use descriptive names for loop variables (task_result, r, param, etc.)
single_key_characteristics: ALWAYS starts with: some attestation in input.attestations
Checks a single property after filtering by task name
Simple condition: task.name == X AND task.property == Y
Example: Check if build task status is Succeeded
compound_characteristics: ALWAYS starts with: some attestation in input.attestations
Loops over ALL tasks (no name filter)
Validates across all tasks in the attestation
Example: Check all tasks have bundle with digest
Example: Check all tasks with parameter X don't have value Y
